articleTitle: High Speed VCSELs and Co-Packaging for Short Reach Communication within Cloud and High Performance Computing
abstract: Directly modulated VCSELs, both shortwave (MMF) and longwave (SMF) continue to advance with speeds reaching 160Gb/s and distances beyond 100m. Co-packaged optics is the next progression from pluggables in the evolution of high speed optical interconnect. This talk will cover both of these topics.

articleTitle: Optimized LED-based Optical Wireless Power Transmission System Configuration for Compact IoT
abstract: For internet-of-things (IoT) terminals, optical wireless power transmission (OWPT) is promising candidate of power supplying, which has advantages such as long transmission. In this paper, optimized configurations of LED-based OWPT system that realized small dimension and large electricity power supply amount for compact IoT terminals is designed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Light-Induced Self-Written Optical Waveguide Fabrication by Near Infrared Continuous Wave Laser Light with Microwatt Power
abstract: We have successfully demonstrated light-induced self-written (LISW) waveguides at a wavelength of 1070 nm and 1310 nm, respectively. Microwatt level photopolymerization threshold value was obtained at both wavelengths. The results show a promising approach for optical interconnection in silicon photonics.

articleTitle: VCSEL Array for 3D Sensing
abstract: In this talk, I will discuss inventions and advances in VCSELs that have led to recent global deployment of commercial applications including 3D sensing and optical coherent tomography applications.

articleTitle: Quantum dot-based optically pumped VCSELs with high-contrast periodic gratings
abstract: We present our recent results on quantum dot-based VCSELs for O-band telecoms applications. The incorporation of Sirich SiN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> distributed Bragg mirrors, which have been studied by spectroscopic ellipsometry, as well as using high-contrast SiN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> 1D gratings will lead to a significant size reduction desirable for the fabrication.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental analysis of power generation characteristics in beam direction control of optical wireless power transmission with mirror
abstract: Numerical and experimental analysis of power generation efficiency of the optical wireless power transmission (OWPT) system with mirror in a room was investigated. It was clarified that using mirror to transfer light to solar cell is useful to compensate the deformation of beam at long distance. In addition, number of mirrors needed in a typical room was investigated.

articleTitle: Characterization and Optimization of Fly-eye Lens System in Optical Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: Fly-eye lens system is advantageous for improving system efficiency in optical wireless power transmission due to achievable of uniform light irradiation pattern. From the experiment, a large tolerance in the lateral direction and the transmission direction was obtained for proposed configuration. Light source position is discussed for high uniformity.

articleTitle: High speed modulation single mode 850 nm DTCC-VCSEL
abstract: We present a novel design of double-transverse-coupled-cavity VCSELs toward high speed modulations of more than 20GHz for single mode operation. In-plane lateral optical feedback in both cavities enables the large bandwidth enhancement of direct modulations. The Vernier effect in DTCC could be a help for single-mode operation in larger oxide apertures.

articleTitle: A Novel Spot-Size Converter with Asymmetric Taper for Deep-Ridge Waveguide Devices
abstract: A novel spot-size converter with a buried asymmetric taper which enables a $0\,\mu \mathrm{m}$-wide tip is proposed for high coupling efficiency between a deep-ridge waveguide device and an optical fiber. As a result of measurement, fabricated devices showed a very low mode conversion and coupling loss of 0.6 dB/facet.

articleTitle: Polymer interconnection waveguide for multi-core fibers using 45° mirror and self-formation lens
abstract: We fabricated a polymer interconnection waveguide aiming for switching between multi-core fibers using 45° mirror and self-formation polymer lens. It can be realized at lower cost by oblique-exposure photolithograph and polymer drop in the hole. According to the analysis results, a very low optical coupling loss would be expected.

articleTitle: Temperature Effects on Dispersion Tailoring of Slow Light Engineered Photonic Crystal Waveguide
abstract: Slow light dispersion in gallium arsenide based twist induced photonic crystal waveguides is presented and the effect of temperature is studied. A shift in the innermost row is resulting with the increase in group index. It is observed that the slowdown region of light is shifting with temperature.

articleTitle: Design of Chirped Focusing Grating Coupler in Nb2O5-based Integrated Probe for Laser Doppler Cross-sectional Velocity Distribution Measurement
abstract: An integrated probe using Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> waveguides is presented for two-dimensional cross-sectional velocity distribution measurements. The chirped focusing grating used for waveguide-air coupling is designed and its efficiency is calculated. The scanning function of the probe using the grating couplers is simulated.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study of Saturation Output Power on Quantum Dot Semiconductor Optical Amplifier (SOA) under High Temperature (85 °C)
abstract: We have studied the saturation output power of 1.3-μm wavelength quantum dot semiconductor optical amplifier (QD-SOA) under high temperature by using Fabry-Pérot laser diode structure. The saturation output power of 5 dBm has been confirmed under 85°C with a single stripe device (375 μm length).

articleTitle: Organic Light Emitting Diodes - For New Era Displays
abstract: Organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs) are on the market for smart phones and televisions. The OLED have a lot of charming points, however, there were still issues. In this time, I would like to present the OLED and my research experiences related to device and optical technologies.

articleTitle: Fabry-Perot Optical Fiber Temperature Sensor using Graded-Index Fiber for Cryotherapy
abstract: We developed a Fabry-Perot interference temperature sensor composed of a graded-index (GI) fiber for cryotherapy. The sensor consists of a single-mode fiber attached to a glass capillary with GI fiber. The sensor shows excellent characteristics at temperatures as low as -43 °C.

articleTitle: Wave Plate Fabrication Using Surface Plasmon Polariton in a Ag Wire Grid Structure
abstract: In this study, a waveplate using surface plasmons in a silver (Ag) wire grid structure is designed and fabricated. Simulation results confirmed a phase difference at a grating period of 360 nm, a duty ratio of 0.7, and an Ag thickness of 30 nm.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control of Injection Current and Temperature at DFB-LD for High-speed High-Reliability Wavelength Switching
abstract: We devise cooperative control of injection current and temperature for wavelength switching at the DFB-LD. Prompt change of the current makes high-speed switching and gradual cooperative change of current/temperature results in wavelength stabilization at lower current. Experiment shows a switching within 31 ms as well as long term stabilization with the current of less than 100 mA.

articleTitle: Effect of radiation dose of Gamma-Ray irradiation on volume gratings using liquid crystal composites
abstract: The radiation-hardened characteristics are important for the optically reconfigurable gate arrays (ORGAs) architecture consisting of a holographic memory part having highly defect tolerant. We investigated the effect of 500 Mrad total-ionizing-dose of Gamma-Ray irradiation on volume gratings using liquid crystal composites. The optical properties and internal grating structures by using a cobalt 60 gamma radiation source were evaluated to produce more radiation-hardened holographic memory.

articleTitle: Simultaneous QAM Conversion of CATV Multi-Channel Signals by Using External Optical Modulators
abstract: Simultaneous QAM conversion of CATV multi-channel signals for the identical broadcast information has been successfully demonstrated by using external optical modulators for the first time. The novel QAM conversion system is assumed to be used for the emergency broadcast and local commercial on CATV multi-channel.

articleTitle: Modulation Format Conversion Between QPSK, OOK and 8QAM Using Optical Nonlinear Effects
abstract: All-optical modulation format conversion method between QPSK, OOK and 8QAM is numerically demonstrated by using nonlinear effects in semiconductor optical amplifier and optical threshold device. As a result, error free format conversion is achieved.

articleTitle: Wavelength Tunable filter with Curved Directional Coupler
abstract: We investigate a structure to reduce the wavelength-dependence of a ring resonator's transmission characteristics by replacing the conventional directional coupler of the racetrack resonator with a curved directional coupler. We show its potential as a filter for broadband wavelength tunable single mode lasers.

articleTitle: Dynamics of a highly sensitive Erbium-doped Fabry-Perot Fiber (EDFBF) Laser Sensor under pump modulation
abstract: This study experimentally investigates changes occurring in a highly sensitive Erbium-doped Fabry-Perot fiber (EDFPF) laser sensor under pump modulation by varying the modulation frequency from 1 kHz to 60 kHz. The dynamic behaviour of the EDFBF laser sensor and the laser spectrum of the routes to chaos are presented graphically.

articleTitle: Glass 3D printing for ultra-miniaturized endoscopic optical systems
abstract: Endoscopy is one of the most widely used medical diagnostic tools for non-invasive in vivo imaging, and advances in micro-optics have radically increased the optical functionality of such probes. We show here how highly-precise freeform three-dimensional structuring of glass may be used to fabricate optomechanical mounting features and complete hermetic packaging for multi-modal optical diagnostic systems on size scales (typically less than 4 mm in diameter) compatible for use in standard endoscopic tools. Complete glass-encapsulated endo-microscopy imagers integrated with a scanning optical coherence tomography system are used as an example for the highly functional, ultra-compact endoscopic probe heads which may be realized with this technology.

articleTitle: Nested Mach-Zehnder Interferometer Optical Switch with Low Crosstalk
abstract: We demonstrate a $1 \times \mathrm {N}$ nested Mach-Zehnder interferometer optical switch configuration with low crosstalk regardless of coupling ratio deviation. It also has an inherent symmetry which helps a scale expansion of its port count.

articleTitle: Effects of Core Aspect-ratio in Bent Buried Si-wire Waveguides
abstract: The imaginary-distance cylindrical full-vectorial BPM is adopted to study the effect of core location in a buried Si-wire waveguide with various aspect ratios. Reduced bend loss is achieved when the air-cladding interface is placed at the position where the field amplitude decays to 5% of its peak.

articleTitle: Influence of Phase Constant Difference between Dispersive Elements in Difference-Frequency Generation Based Optical-Phase-Conjugation Circuit
abstract: Influence of phase constant difference between two dispersive elements in difference-frequency generation based opticalphase-conjugator is theoretically studied. Calculation results show a slight change of a phase constant due to refractive index change with 1.0 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> order severely affects output phase-conjugated signal power.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Modulation Responses of Directly Modulated Lasers with Passive Feedback and Partially Corrugated Grating
abstract: The modulation response of a high-speed directly modulated laser (DML) is enhanced by integrating a passive feedback section to reduce the waveform distortions that is critical for PAM-4 modulation. The partially corrugated grating (PCG) structure helps to maintain >85% single-mode yield under passive feedback.

articleTitle: Adaptive Compensation for Atmospheric Turbulence in Orbital Angular Momentum Free Space Optical Transmission System
abstract: We evaluated the adaptive compensation method for the influence of atmospheric turbulence in free space optical (FSO) communication using orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam by numerical simulation. We found that using the pilot beam of the same azimuthal index to the data beam could effectively compensate for the influence.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact 3D measurement module using silica-based PLC
abstract: We fabricated the world's smallest optical module using a silica-based planar lightwave circuit for performing three-dimensional measurements. The module with a fiber, a camera and a lens is so small as to be attached to a 2.5 mm tube. We demonstrated accurate shape measurements with a variation of 0.1 mm.

articleTitle: Optical wireless power transmission of applying OAM and adaptive optics
abstract: With the spread of 5G, studies on OAM multiplex transmission that enhances frequency utilization efficiency in wireless communications are progressing, and a technology that can supply power while realizing these is required. In this study, we tried to improve power loss and transmission characteristics due to atmospheric turbulence by applying adaptive optics and Laguerre Gaussian mode.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarization Effects in Sheared Two-Dimensional Grating Couplers for Silicon Photonics
abstract: We analyse the cross-polarization in sheared two-dimensional grating couplers. As key parameters, the waveguide-to-grating shear angle and the etch depth are considered. Numerical and experimental results show that the cross-polarization is a limiting factor of crucial importance for both coupling efficiency and polarization-splitting functionality.

articleTitle: Controlled Generation of Isolated C-points in Few-mode Optical Fiber
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the controlled generation of isolated C-points such as Lemon, Star and Monstar in a few-mode optical fiber by controlling the coupling conditions. We also study the effect of relative phase difference between interfering modes on the generation of C-points.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Cross-Sectional Velocity Distribution Measurements Using Laser Doppler Velocimeter Employing 7 × 8 Spatial Encoding
abstract: A laser Doppler velocimeter employing 7×8-channel spatially encoded measurement points is proposed for simultaneous cross-sectional velocity distribution measurements. The measurement points arranged in two dimensions are encoded by combining wavelength-division multiplexing and multiple bias-frequency encoding. The functionality of the proposed method was experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Aerial Display on a Clear Sphere with Aerial Imaging by Retro-Reflection
abstract: This paper deals with a method to form an aerial image on a clear sphere. Two clear spheres are installed in an optics for aerial imaging by retro-reflection. We investigate the distribution of light incident on retro-reflector and also magnification effect of difference of clear spheres in size.

articleTitle: High-voltage CMOS photovoltaic module with Schottky bypass diodes
abstract: We demonstrate monolithic integration of high-voltage photovoltaic array and Schottky bypass diodes on the same bulk CMOS chip for the first time. Post localized substrate removal process was utilized to enable on-chip electrical isolation and serial/parallel connection. Assembled PV module provides an output voltage of 4.19V and is less sensitive to the optical shading.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fiber Based Emitting Head for Optical Wireless Communication
abstract: A fiber based emitting head for optical wireless communication (OWC) is proposed and experimentally evaluated. We analysed the characterization of emitting head by experiment and simulation software. The method of beam expanded was achieved by using an arc curvature design which was acted as a microlenses.

articleTitle: Suppression of fiber fuse initiation by amplitude modulation of input light
abstract: We propose a new method for suppressing fiber fuse initiation in conventional single-mode fibers (SMFs). We experimentally demonstrate that the initiation of fiber fuse can be suppressed in a SMF by using amplitude modulation of the input light when the input power is 5 W.

articleTitle: High-Extinction-Ratio Multiple Quantum Well Modulator Based on Multimode Interference Waveguide
abstract: We proposed an optical modulator based on a multiple quantum well (MQW) multimode interference (MMI) waveguide. A partial electrode region is asymmetrically placed in an MMI waveguide. Owing to the combination of the electroabsorption effect and change in the electrorefractive index in the MQW, the extinction ratio is significantly improved.

articleTitle: Improving the quality of decrypted signal in an encryption system for secure free-space optical communication
abstract: The quality of a decrypted signal depends on the two intensity patterns of the input signal, which correspond to the 1-bit states “1” and “0,” in a two-dimensional encryption system. In this study, we discuss via simulations the selection of spatial patterns to improve the decrypted signals.

articleTitle: Secure Digital-domain Symbol Masking Using Four-level Phase-shift-based twobit Block-ciphering for Coherent QPSK Transmission
abstract: We propose two-bit-block to four-level phase shift-based symbol-masking at the post-symbol mapper, which can double the bit information amount of encryption key per symbol, and experimentally demonstrate a secure 10 Gsymbol/s QPSK system using a proposed symbol masking scheme.

articleTitle: Fiber fuse terminator consisting of a step-index multimode fiber spliced with SMFs
abstract: We propose a fiber fuse terminator consisting of a commercially available short length of step-index multimode fiber, spliced with conventional SMFs. The fabricated fiber fuse terminator suppressed the fiber fuse propagation when the input power was 6 W, at a wavelength of 1.55 μm.

articleTitle: Design of Free-Form Light Intensity Distribution Control Element for High-Brightness Projectors Using Solid-State Light Sources
abstract: A light intensity distribution control element having a free-form surface shape for projectors in which blue lasers and yellow phosphors are combined was designed. This element improves the light utilization efficiency by transforming the shape of the light beam from circular to rectangular and makes the light intensity distribution uniform.

articleTitle: Observation of 60 GHz and 20 GHz Multiple Photon-Photon Resonances Using Active Multimode Interferometer Laser Diodes
abstract: We have designed and fabricated 1 × N active multimode interferometer laser diodes to achieve two photon-photon resonances (PPRs). Very high frequency of 60 GHz in addition to 20 GHz PPR peaks were confirmed.

articleTitle: All-fiber imaging system for ultra-thin flexible endoscope based on compressed image reconstruction
abstract: A single-fiber imaging system which is robust to fiber bending is proposed. The imaging system is all-fiber optics based on a double-clad fiber. The image reconstruction by using proposed system is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A random laser with tunable threshold by bending curvature
abstract: We investigate the case that the transport mean free path of emitted photons within the disordered scatterers, which is composed by the ZnO nanowires, is tunable by a curvature bending applied on the flexible substrate underneath, thereby creating a unique light source which is able to be operated above and below the lasing threshold for desirable spectral emissions.

articleTitle: Bistable tuning operation in an Nb2O5 DBR resonator with ferroelectric liquid crystal cladding
abstract: We fabricated an Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> tunable waveguide resonator with ferroelectric liquid crystal. The design and characteristics of the fabricated devices are reported herein. Bistable tuning operation with a 2.2-nm shift in wavelength characteristics was obtained.

articleTitle: Study of Plasmonic Nanolasers with Graphene–Metal Interaction
abstract: The charge transfer effect of the graphene-oxide-metal interface on the performance of plasmonic nanolasers was investigated. The results show that the variation of electron densities of metals can influence the characteristics of surface-plasmon-polariton modes and lead to a significant improvement in the performance of plasmonic nanolasers.

articleTitle: Plasmonic nanolasers based on graphene-insulator-metal platform
abstract: As the development of nanoscale optics, the ability of surface plasmons to break the diffraction limit receives numerous attention from researchers. In this work, we demonstrate a graphene-insulator-metal (GIM) nanolaser structure. The graphene can modify the permittivity of metal films which would further influence the nanolasers characteristics.

articleTitle: Time of Flight 3D Imaging using VCSEL Beam Scanner
abstract: We demonstrated a non-mechanical beam-scanning LiDAR system based on a VCSEL beam scanner. We measured a target object at a distance of 20m with depth measurement accuracy of 30cm. The peak-power of the beam scanner is as small as 160mW, which shows a potential of extending the distance range by increasing the power.

articleTitle: Studies on fiber coupling characteristics of received beam by transmission-type holographic optical element for free-space optical communications
abstract: The use of a holographic optical element as the substitution of the fine pointing mechanism in free-space optical communications is proposed. The coupling characteristics of the transmission-type hologram to a single mode fiber is experimentally investigated to show its advantage to the use of the reflection-type.

articleTitle: Optical Response Measurements of R/G/B Mini-LEDs with Short Pulse Voltage
abstract: This paper demonstrates the rising and falling response time behaviour for low power RGB mini-LEDs. By biasing these LEDs with external clock signal, behaviour such as exponential decay were observed at some pulse edges of the output signals. The exponential decay for different low power input signals were analysed and the causes of such phenomenon were conclude in this paper.

articleTitle: Incident-Angle-Dependence-Relaxed Polarization Grating formed using Polymer Liquid Crystal Exhibiting Biaxial Optical Anisotropy
abstract: In this work, a polarization grating in Raman-Nath regime was fabricated by using a photoreactive polymer liquid crystal exhibiting biaxial optical anisotropy. And from the measured characteristics, it has been demonstrated that the flat incident angle dependences on diffraction efficiency and polarization ellipticity are obtained by introducing biaxial optical anisotropy.

articleTitle: Improved Light Extraction of Organic Light Emission Diodes With ZnO-Nanorod Structure
abstract: In order to improve a light outcoupling efficiency in bottom emission organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), an interfacial layer of ZnO nanorod was grown on an outside of glass substrate. The ZnO structure have nano-sized bump structure and higher refractive index of around 2.1. Light extraction of OLED was improved to be more than 150%. This ZnO structure is useful for lower temperature fabrication and simple process just only growing on the ZnO using solution process without patterning.

articleTitle: High-power-output (11 dBm) SOA assisted extended reach EADFB laser (AXEL) for 1.25-Gbit/s high-loss budget optical access networks
abstract: A high-power SOA assisted extended reach EADFB laser was fabricated for high-loss budget access network systems. The modulation output power was 11 dBm with an extinction ratio of 10.3 dB. We obtained error-free 80-km single-mode fiber transmissions at a signal rate of 1.25-Gbit/s with a power budget of 48 dB.

articleTitle: Simulation of microoptics under inhomogeneous illumination: Sinusoidal Phase Grating under Gaussian Beam Illumination
abstract: Far field pattern generation is investigated for thick sinusoidal phase grating under a Gaussian beam illumination to obtain a high field of view. We compare the Fraunhofer approximation with the High-NA propagator and demonstrate that the Fraunhofer approximation is not valid for thick phase gratings.

articleTitle: The mechanism of H2 plasma in III-nitride low-temperature epitaxy
abstract: Inductively coupled plasma MOCVD (ICP-MOCVD) is proposed for III-nitride low temperature epitaxy and the mechanism of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma during the epitaxy has been studied. The reduction of C, H and O impurities and the etching of GaN films were observed by introducing H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma in the epitaxy process.

articleTitle: Efficient decoding method for M-ary OAM shift keying in FSO link
abstract: We investigated two kinds of decoding methods for our proposed 8-ary orbital angular momentum shift keying technique in FSO communication link with atmospheric turbulence. At transmitter side, decoding of transmitting information is very important because transmitted beam distorted by atmospheric turbulence.

articleTitle: Inscription and Optimization of Fibre-Optic Long Period Gratings Using Electric Arc Discharge
abstract: In this work, we report on recent results about the inscription and optimization of Long Period Gratings (LPG), by means of electric arc discharge technique. We have optimized the proper combination of arc time and arc power which allows appropriate core and cladding modulation for desired LPG spectral features.

articleTitle: Influence of the f/# in wavefront coding with Jacobi Fourier phase masks
abstract: Jacoby Fourier polynomial shaped phase masks (JFPM) have been shown to be potentially effective for extending the depth of focus in wavefront coding technique. However, some characteristics have not been reported in detail. Here, we will show performance of JFPM for different f/# and compare with the trefoil phase mask.

articleTitle: The Surface Emitting Laser Turned of Light: Everybody Has It
abstract: The VCSEL(Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser) is a new type of semiconductor laser and now generating new applications such as high-speed local area networks, computer mice, parallel optical interconnects, laser printers, face recognition systems, and various optical sensors.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Interrogation Method for Strain Monitoring in Bridge Beams
abstract: A low cost structural health monitoring method based on fiber Bragg grating sensors is proposed. A long period grating is used as an edge filter and a trans-impedance amplifier is used for the low cost detection of strain monitoring. Proposed method is compact in size and accurate for strain measurement.

articleTitle: Investigation of excitation beam modulation using azimuthal polarization to improve STED resolution
abstract: To improve the resolution of the CW STED microscope using azimuthally modulated excitation beam modulation, phase retardation and various aperture conditions are simulated and tested. The ring-shaped aperture improves lateral resolution while suppressing axial direction elongation, making it suitable for 3D superresolution imaging of STED microscopy.

articleTitle: Micro- and Nano-Structures for High-End Optics
abstract: Novel technology developments allow the fabrication of optical micro- and nano-structures on application relevant areas with extreme precision and high flexibility. The contribution reviews the technological challenges, demonstrates suitable solutions, and gives an insight into today's high-end applications of such lithographically realized structures.

articleTitle: Biophotonic Imaging and Sensing
abstract: In this session, we discuss the past, present and future of biophotonic imaging and sensing technology for applications ranging from in vitro imaging to optical sensing of hard to detect small biomolecules.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Synthesis of Transition Metal Oxides and Polymer Layers for OPV Fabrication
abstract: This paper reports a new method for organic photovoltaic (OPV) fabrication by using the electrochemical synthesis of different transition metal oxides (MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, ZnO, TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>,V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>) and polymers (PEDOT:PSS, P 3HT). Especially two materials are presented: MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and PEDOT:PSS. The integration of this procedure in a roll-to-roll (R2R) process enables the production of a low-cost OPV with high efficiencies.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Detection using Cellular Resolution Optical Coherence Tomography
abstract: The detection of skin cancers has been studied using the full-field optical coherence tomography. High-speed CMOS camera with high brightness light source were employed to achieve real-time imaging with cellular resolution for the detection of cellular atypia and structural derangement. Animal model on squamous cell carcinoma shows greater than 90% accuracy.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Bending Measurement Using Multicore Fiber Bragg Grating and Two-Photon Absorption Process in Si-APD
abstract: We successfully realized three-dimensional bending measurement using multi-core fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) and two-photon absorption (TPA) process in a silicon avalanche photodiode. By the TPA-based distance measurement along with laser wavelength scanning, we identified the FBGs in four cores having almost the same Bragg wavelength and measured their reflection spectra.

articleTitle: Beam Waist Controlled Vertical Optical Path Conversion Using Integrated Curved Micro Mirror for Silicon Photonics
abstract: Curved micro mirrors for silicon-photonics vertical optical coupling were integrated on a silicon substrate by gray-tone optical lithography. Beam waist of the reflected light was successfully controlled by tuning the curvatures of the mirror. The beam waist conversion effect was also confirmed by a coupling efficiency measurement.

articleTitle: Polarization control ofGaN-based micro-caivty lasers with top high-contrast grating reflectors
abstract: We reported on GaN micro-cavity (MC) lasers combining one rigid TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> high-contrast grating (HCG) structure as the output mirror. HCG structure was made directly on the GaN without an airgap, designed to yield high reflectance for transverse magnetic (TM) or transverse electric (TE) polarized light. The laser emission was TM polarized with a degree of polarization of 99.2% and had a small divergence angle of 14 degrees (full width at half maximum), under pulsed optical pumping at room temperature. This demonstration of laser operation for the GaN-based MC with an HCG fully exhibited advantages of HCGs for applications in semiconductor lasers at the wavelength from green to ultraviolet regimes.

articleTitle: Infrared LED Marker for Target Recognition in Optical Wireless Power Transmission to Moving Object at Dark Environment Condition
abstract: Optical Wireless Power Transmission (OWPT) is one of the methods to transmit power wirelessly to long distance. In this research, we use infrared LED marker which is attached on moving object to recognize the target. Using this method, we can demonstrate OWPT to moving object in dark condition.

articleTitle: Thin Multi-Aperture Microscope
abstract: The design and the set-up of a thin multi-aperture microscope is introduced. It utilizes an array of identical micro-optical channels, each magnifying a limited field of view onto a CMOS camera as detector array. The very compact system can capture a large field of view by microscopic lateral scanning.

articleTitle: Dopant dependence of fiber fuse propagation threshold
abstract: We found that a pure silica core fiber had a higher fiber fuse propagation threshold (1.7 W) than a single-mode fiber with the same mode field diameter (MFD). Furthermore, a propagation threshold as high as 2 W was obtained in a fluorine-doped core fiber with an MFD of 10.5 μm.

articleTitle: Adjoint-based Optimization for Diffractive Beam-Splitters
abstract: Computational optimization of diffractive elements is often limited by a large number of design parameters. Adjoint method allows the gradient of target function respect to all design variables to be calculated with only two electromagnetic simulations. We show that detail results for optimized two-dimensional fan-out gratings.

articleTitle: Sensing by Light: Introduction
abstract: In this session, we discuss on the sensing teclmology using laser and light rangin g the detection of neutrinos and gravitational wave, LiDAR for mobiles, 3D face recognition, bio-photonic imaging.

articleTitle: Biosensing Resolution Enhancement on Optical Low Coherence Interferometry through Stepper Motor Stage
abstract: A SPR interferometric phases are typically manipulated with the analyte index change through the effective reaction length and operating wavelengths, respectively, from fiber based optical-low-coherence-interferometry (OLCI) and spectral interferometry for biosensing. The OLCI stepper motor stage built with 0.2-nm moving limit owns potential to achieve a 70-pM sensing resolution.

articleTitle: High-Speed Electro-Optics Based on Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
abstract: Recent development in lithium niobate nanofabrication technology has led to devices with ultra-low optical losses, opening up opportunities for a range of high-performance integrated photonic devices. This talk will discuss our recent results in lithium niobate nanophotonics, including ultra-high-Q microresonators, high-speed integrated modulators, and electro-optic frequency comb generation.

articleTitle: Shape measurement using digital holography with a close set of two wavelengths
abstract: New type of optical system for low-coherence digital holography with a close set of two wavelengths is proposed to measure a shape measurement of a curved surface object with a height of several-tens micrometer. The optical system simultaneously captures the object image with two wavelengths.

articleTitle: Glass-Based Optics For the Connected World
abstract: We are witnessing an incredible era of exponential growth in applications that require advances in materials technology: from 3D printing, to AR/VR to autonomous cars to 5G to machine learning and artificial intelligence, for example. Revolutionary new products are steadily coming into the marketplace and many more are needed and expected. Novel materials play a key role in many of these new products: new displays, new personal mobile devices, new sensors in cars, and new information technology products for both storage and data processing. This talk will focus on the use of glass materials to produce key optical components in display, interconnect and consumer products.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of Harmonic Optical Quantizer
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated optical quantization with same number of optical filters as the number of bits for equipment reduction. Optical filters were designed to obtain 1-bit optical quantization characteristics that have a harmonic relationship by self- frequency shift due to self-phase modulation. We report the effective number of bits was 2. 8bit in three-bit optical quantization.

articleTitle: Hybrid Refraction-Diffraction Optical Element of Side-Absorption Concentrated Array System for Photovoltaic-Thermal Hybrid Applications
abstract: The hybrid refraction-diffraction optical element (HRDOE) of the side-absorption concentrated array system (SCAS) for photovoltaic-thermal hybrid applications is carried out. In order to meet the requirements of spectral division for photovoltaic-thermal applications, thinner volume, light weight and wider acceptance angle, the proposed system integrates the HRDOE array and planar light-guide array. The functions of the HRDOE are to separate the visible and infrared spectra of the incident sunlight and to focus the separated beams. Those focal spots are on the corresponding micro-structure of planar light-guide array, while the beams are then directed to the side surfaces and received by the corresponding energy cells.

articleTitle: Widening the Polarization Conversion Properties of an L-figured Si-wire Waveguide
abstract: A design guideline is presented for a polarization rotator consisting of an L-figured Si-wire waveguide that has a wide bandwidth with low insertion loss. An extinction ratio of more than 20dB is achieved with an insertion loss of less than 1dB over a wavelength range of 1.3 to 1.6 μm.

articleTitle: Micron-Ordered Optical Interference Organic Light Emitting Diodes with Patterned Structure
abstract: Organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs) are now practical use for televisions, smartphones, and micro-displays. Minimum pixel size was miniaturized to several-micron gradually without patterning.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous integration in silicon photonics through micro-transfer-printing
abstract: Micro-transfer-printing enables the intimate integration of a wide range of opto-electronic micro-components on a silicon photonics platform. This technique allows for wafer-scale integration in a massively parallel manner with high alignment accuracy, high throughput and high yield, therefore leading to a cost reduction of complex photonic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Light for Detecting Neutrinos and Gravitational Waves
abstract: More than 30 years ago, Kamiokande experiment began in the underground of Kamioka, Japan. It was a large detector with 3000 ton of water and 1000 photomultiplier tubes. It was designed to observe proton decays. However, proton decays were not observed. Therefore, Prof. Masatoshi Koshiba proposed to modify the detector to observe solar neutrinos. In fact, after the detector improvement, Kamiokande observed neutrinos from a supernova explosion and solar neutrinos. Because of the importance of the studies of these neutrinos, Super-Kamiokande was constructed. Super-Kamiokande is a very large neutrino detector with 50,000 ton of water and 13,000 photomultiplier tubes. The experiment began in 1996. In 1998, neutrino oscillation was discovered by the studies of atmospheric neutrinos. Further studies on neutrinos are in progress in Kamioka. Gravitational waves are generated by the violent motion of heavy mass. Therefore, gravitational waves are expected to be a very important new tool to observe the Universe such as the mergers of blackhole binaries or those of neutron star binaries. In fact, gravitational waves have been observed in the LIGO and Virgo laser interferometers. KAGRA is a project trying to observe gravitational waves with 3 km × 3 km arm lengths laser interferometer. It has been constructed in the underground of Kamioka, Japan. KAGRA has unique features such as the underground site to minimize the effect of seismic noises and the cryogenic mirrors to reduce the thermal noises.

articleTitle: Reduction of optical background noise in BOCDA distributed strain measurement technology by synthesizing frequency modulation waveform of light source
abstract: Brillouin optical correlation domain analysis has already presented high performance. However, it makes the system configuration complicated. We propose a method that simplifies the system configuration by synthesizing frequency modulation waveform of light source. In the experiment, we can suppress the background noise while simplifying the system.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Scanning Photocurrent Microscopy in Ultra-Thin Silicon Nanowire Ohmic-Contact Devices
abstract: The feasibility of the carrier decay length extraction from scanning photocurrent profiles in ultra-thin silicon nanowire ohmic-contact devices is theoretically studied. Accurate carrier decay length can be extracted with a typical diffraction-limited excitation spot size of 500 nm for silicon nanowires with diameter down to 20 nm.

articleTitle: Application of Scattering Characteristics to Module with Filters on Solar Cell for Improvement of OWPT Equipment Appearance
abstract: Optical wireless power transmission (OWPT) systems are attractive photonic systems based on light sources and solar cells. To improve the visual appearance of practical consumer applications, we have applied visible color filters to change the typical black appearance of solar cells. We also used frosted glass to change the roughness of the surface to achieve light scattering which is important for good appearance. The results show that the OWPT system can change its appearance with an acceptable slight deterioration in performance.

articleTitle: Real-Time Displacement Measurement Based on Intensity Correlation Between Reflected Probe Light and Phase Modulated Signal
abstract: We proposed and investigated real-time displacement measurement using intensity correlation between reflected probe light and phase modulated signal. The optical system was designed to suppress the noise due to interference with stray light. Real-time displacement measurement of a target moving at 1 mm/s or 10 mm/s was successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Fine Porous Structures Fabricated from Poly(vinyl alcohol)-Coated Polystyrene Templates for Functional Biosensing Chips
abstract: Sensitive and functional biosensor chips are required to detect various molecules or substances. We have developed a fabrication process for an unique porous structure which was fabricated from poly(vinyl alcohol)-coated polystyrene template. In this study, the formation mechanism such porous structure is investigated in detail.

articleTitle: Reflective Silicon Arrayed Waveguide Grating using One-Dimensional Photonic Crystal reflector
abstract: We report silicon arrayed waveguide grating with reflective fan-out geometry using one-dimensional photonic crystal as reflector. Wide reflection spectral range is possible with this reflector. The wavelength characteristics are obtained by fabricated device using immersion ArF lithography. We also report a device using parallel waveguide array geometry to minimize the occupational area of the device.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocity Enhancement of Graphene-on-Si Waveguide using One-Dimensional Photonic Crystal
abstract: The effect of using one-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide on the nonreciprocity of graphene-on-silicon waveguides is theoretically investigated. It is shown that the position of air-hole strongly affects the loss of forward and backward propagation modes.

articleTitle: Cobalt Ferrite Films Deposited on Silicon with Magnesium Oxide Buffer Layer for Silicon Photonics Magneto-optic Devices
abstract: CoFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> films were grown on (100)-Si substrates with a MgO buffer layer for silicon photonics applications. Both CoFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and MgO films were deposited by RF magnetron sputtering. The structural analysis reveals that CoFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> films grown with an MgO buffer layer have a single-oriented structure.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Improvement of Step-index Multimode Fiber Using Variable Mode Scramble Device
abstract: We have successfully improved the transmission bandwidth of a step-index multimode fiber by applying torsional stress to the fiber using a variable mode scrambler device. At this time, the maximum radiation angle of the far-field pattern of the fiber did not change with the torsional stress.

articleTitle: Monolithic Integration of MEMS Tunable VCSEL and Beam Deflector
abstract: We propose a laterally integrated beam deflector with MEMS tunbale VCSEL, which offers high resolutions and high power operation. The modelling shows a large beam deflection angle of over 37°. We fabricated integrated devices with an MEMS actuator composed of dielectric DBR layers. A deflection angle of 6.4° was obtained with a wavelength change of 3.4nm.

articleTitle: High Speed and Low Power Consumption, Thermo-optic Phase Shifter
abstract: We propose a thermo-optic phase shifter which uses multimode interference. Electrodes are attached to the section where the multimode interference has minimum optical power in the sidewalls. We use the Silicon large thermo-optic constant to create an integrated optical device to control the state of light in several microseconds, for both heating and cooling times.

articleTitle: 100 °C deposited transparent silicon nitride film for O-band photonic applications
abstract: A transparent silicon nitride film deposited at 100 °C is developed by liquid-source chemical vapor deposition (LSCVD) method. With a combination of the series of spectrometric analysis, we reveal that the waveguide shows low propagation loss (~1.0 dB/cm) with practically applicable high refractive index (~1.85) in the O-band (1260-1360 nm).

articleTitle: Compact and High Sensitive Swgms Bragg Grating on Soi Platform for Refractive Index Sensing
abstract: We propose Bragg grating (BG) refractive index sensor composed of sub-wavelength grating multi-slot (SWGMS) waveguides with single etch-step fabrication. To improve performances two-type gratings in a period are studied. Our simulated structure has length of 17.27 μm, a sensitivity (S) 663 nm/RIU and an extinction ratio (ER) of 29.7 dB.

articleTitle: Transmission Performance of 16QAM Signal Interleaved with Amplified Reference Light
abstract: M-ary modulated signals interleaved with amplified reference light is proposed and numerically investigated. The proposed method improves chromatic dispersion tolerance, and transmittable distance of 10-Gbuad interleaved 16QAM signals is extended by 2.46 times compared to the conventional systems.

articleTitle: Light Receiving Characteristics from Air to Underwater Optical Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: Optical wireless power transmission (OWPT) has attracted a lot of attention, and underwater OWPT will become an important application. In this report, we simulated the light distribution underwater, and carried out the experiment of the model that light incident from air to underwater. It was clarified that the light spread and time dependent output fluctuation are important characteristics of OWPT passing through the waves.

articleTitle: Novel Si Photonic Waveguides and Applications to Optical Modulators
abstract: We employed anisotropic wet-etching to define Si wire, slot, and fin waveguides with low propagation loss for optical modulator applications. In a photonic crystal with broken mirror symmetry, we found an opening of a band gap with the mode profile similar to graphene and poly-acetylene made of vortices with topological charge.

articleTitle: Cross-stacking of Guided-mode Resonance Gratings for Polarization-independent Flat-top Filtering
abstract: A stack of two thin film waveguide gratings was designed to provide polarization-independent flat-top filtering for a vertically incident free-space wave. The grating was fabricated by a relief of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> on a Si-N guiding core layer on a SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> substrate. Predicted filtering performance was experimentally demonstrated with 7-nm bandwidth.

articleTitle: High-Speed Wide-Range Wavelength Switching for Tunable Distributed Amplification (TDA-) DFB Laser Based on Nonlinear Model
abstract: The TDA-DFB laser has nonlinearity on the current-wavelength characteristic and needs high accuracy control model for realizing high-speed wide-range switching We designed a nonlinear model for high-speed 600-GHz-wide wavelength switching and showed the feasibility of this control model for much wider range switching.

articleTitle: Investigation on Ultra-Low Voltage Quantum Well Optical Modulator for Optical Interconnection for Superconducting Integrated Circuits
abstract: We propose an ultra-low voltage modulator for optical interconnection in a superconducting Josephson-CMOS hybrid system. By using an InGaAs/InAlAs quantum well microring resonator-enhanced Mach-Zehnder modulator, an operating voltage as low as 0.6 mV is expected with the modulation speed of over 10 GHz at cryogenic temperature.

articleTitle: Waveguide Integrated Organic Laser Source for Lab-on-Chip Applications
abstract: Organic lasers are promising laser sources when it comes to downsizing and flexibility. Especially Lab-on-Chip and sensor applications which are based on ridge waveguide systems face the challenge of an efficient light coupling into the waveguide network. In this paper, we report on the successful integration of organic lasers into polymeric ridge waveguides.

articleTitle: Topological Insulator Laser
abstract: We describe the recent progress on topological insulator lasers, where we employed the fundamental concepts of topological insulators in the non-Hermitian laser system, to force an array of many semiconductor (InGaAs) resonators to lock together and act as one coherent laser source.

articleTitle: Compact fluorescence endoscope with speckle-generating fiber probe
abstract: A thin fiber-optic probe was designed and fabricated for endoscopic fluorescence imaging using the speckle-illumination and compressed sensing. The fiber-optic probe was composed of bundled multi-mode fibers, which generated structured illumination and collected fluorescence signal from the sample. The fluorescence image reconstruction by inserting the fiber probe into the biopsy channel of a conventional colonoscope was also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Consideration of All-Optical Modulation Format Conversion From BPSK to QPSK in Free-Space Communication Using OAM Beam
abstract: This paper considers an issue of phase error in the all-optical modulation format conversion from BPSK to QPSK in free-space communication using OAM beam. Numerical simulation reveals that the phase error affects the constellation of the converted signal and the performance evaluated by error vector magnitude.

articleTitle: Effective Localization of Brillouin Dynamic Grating for Distributed Fiber Sensing by Intensity-Modulated Correlation-Domain Technique
abstract: We proposed an effective localization method of Brillouin dynamic grating for fiber strain/temperature distributed sensing using intensity-modulated correlation-domain technique. Theoretical and experimental results show that our scheme significantly improves the spatial resolution performance of the reflection spectrum of dynamic grating.

articleTitle: Local tuning of transfer-printed quantum-dot single-photon sources on a CMOS silicon chip
abstract: We report local wavelength tuning of quantum-dot single-photon sources integrated on a CMOS silicon chip as well as in-situ spectral matching between two dissimilar sources. All the necessary heterogeneous integration processes were performed in a simple pick-and-place manner based on transfer printing, largely facilitating the fabrication of complicated device structures.

articleTitle: Patterned emission of organic light emitting diodes with laser irradiation
abstract: We have researched on patterned emission of organic light-emitting diodes. The organic layer was deposited followed by laser patterning in atmosphere. The laser irradiation part was quenched, and it was shown that arbitrary patterning was possible. This technique is expected as a fabrication technique for an on-demand pattern emission.

articleTitle: Tunable optical filters using artificial muscles
abstract: We present a new generation of tunable optical filters in the mid-infrared range using Liquid Crystal Elastomers (LCEs), a form of “artificial muscle”, for actuation. LCEs are elastomer-based materials which exhibit directionally-programmable strain of up to 50% and may thus be used to generate large stroke movements. The Fabry-Pérot-based tunable filter has a tuning range of 290 nm around a central wavelength of 4.5 μm. The spectral width of the transmission peak is 165 nm; power consumption is 520 mW. We discuss the system design, fabrication, measurement and evaluation of this novel type of tunable device.

articleTitle: Plano-concave mini-lens array for plenoptic imaging applications
abstract: An array of plano-concave mini-lenses is designed to realize a particular version of Light Field camera known as Plenoptic Camera 1.2. The Delano diagram related to the on-axis optical channel of such a camera is computed to show its retro-focus behavior and it is compared with the Delano diagrams of the Galilean and Keplerian configurations.

articleTitle: Athermal Silicon Ring Resonators with TiO2 Hybrid-Polymer Claddings
abstract: Thermo-optic coefficients of organic-inorganic hybrid polymers with rutile-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles were carefully estimated using SOI ring resonators. Athermal operation of the SOI ring resonators with TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> hybrid-polymer claddings was achieved. The hybrid-polymer cladding can be applied to diverse silicon waveguide structures to control the temperature dependence of silicon photonic devices.

articleTitle: A Cluster of Grating Couplers for Input Coupling of Mixed Wavefronts
abstract: An integrated-optic device is proposed and discussed for coupling almost-vertically-incident free-space waves of different propagation angles to single mode waveguides. Coupling coefficient is varied in the coupling aperture in order to give high input-coupling efficiency. A design example is shown for a SOI waveguide with -6dB coupling efficiency.

articleTitle: Luminescence Investigation of Magnesium Stannate Phosphors Films
abstract: We experimentally investigate the luminescence of Ti-doped magnesium stannate (Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>:Ti) phosphor films via a sol-gel spin coating. The films exhibit blue-light emission with peaking at 440 nm under UV excitation. The emission intensity of films was dependent upon the dopant and number of coating layer.

articleTitle: Speckle measurement for light diffusion fiber
abstract: The speckle of the diffusion optical fiber using a laser light source was evaluated. A new method was used to measure the speckle of curved surfaces and small areas of thin fiber. In addition, depending on the fiber structure, the speckle effect was found to depend on the measurement angle.

articleTitle: A Broadband PLC-type Mode Converter Designed by Wavefront Matching Method
abstract: A broadband multimode-interference-type LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11a</sub> mode converter is proposed for silica PLC platform. A wavefront matching method is used to optimize the waveguide geometry for broadband operation. Numerical simulations show that the conversion efficiency is larger than -1.8 dB from 1.3 to 1.7 μm.

articleTitle: Snapshot-type CCD spectrometer utilizing distributed passband-type multichannel photonic crystal wavelength filter array
abstract: A compact and versatile snapshot-type multi-channel spectrometer was constructed by mounting a patterned spectral filter array onto a CCD area sensor. The individual filter element is consisted of a wavy Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> multilayer (2-D photonic crystal) fabricated by the rf-bias sputtering process. By utilizing the distributed passband characteristics of the filter and the spectral estimation algorithm (Wiener estimation method), we confirmed that the incoming spectra at red to near infrared band could be estimated with good accuracy. We investigated the measurement performance for fruits, which is one of the most important targets of the near infrared spectroscopy, by simulating the realistic condition with optical shot noise.

articleTitle: Rapid thickness and optoelectronic properties characterization of few-layer 2D materials based on hyperspectral microscopy
abstract: We present a technique to efficiently identify the thickness and properties of typical 2D materials. By taking microscopic images at a series wavelengths, we obtain reflectance, transmittance and absorption spectra in a single step. We demonstrate using the setup to unambiguously determine the thickness of MoS2 flakes and their excitonic properties.

articleTitle: Progress in Photonic-Crystal Lasers
abstract: Photonic-crystal lasers have attracted much attention for their unrivaled capabilities, such as broad-area, coherent resonance, tailored beam patterns, and two-dimensional (2D) beam scanning. In this conference, we describe the recent progress of photonic crystal lasers including high-brightness operation, 2D beam scanning operation, and extension to GaN systems.

articleTitle: A Renaissance in Brillouin Photonics for On-Chip Signal Processing and Sensing
abstract: The objectives are to develop the experimental and theoretical expertise to design and build linear and nonlinear all-optical signal processing devices, and to miniaturize these, leading to a photonics chip believed to be the building blocks for the next generation of optical systems.

articleTitle: Extreme Nonlinear Optics in Epsilon-near-zero Materials
abstract: We demonstrate extreme nonlinear optical properties leveraging epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) effect in plasmonic conductive metal oxide thin films. With the aid of high-mobility indium-doped cadmium oxide as the gateway plasmonic material, we show ultrafast all-optical switching and efficient UV high-harmonic generation.

articleTitle: Wavelength Characteristics of a Silicon Waveguide Mach-Zehnder Interferometer having a Ce:YIG cladding
abstract: Ce:YIG thin films deposited on the silicon substrates were fabricated and their crystalline quality was investigated. In addition, a silicon waveguide Mach-Zehnder interferometer having a crystallized Ce:YIG cladding was fabricated. The transmitted wavelength characteristic of the device was observed to be different depending on the magnetostatic field direction.

articleTitle: Computational Ghost Image via Controlling Pseudothermal Light Source
abstract: In this study, we implemented a two-step setup to validate the ghost image through the coherent argument. Here we applied a SLM-based pseudothermal point source and sequentially scanned through the object. By means of 2nd - order VCZ theory, we can retrieve the original object subject to different propagation distances.

articleTitle: Multipoint Sensing Measurement using Optical Fiber Refractive Index Sensors Driven by Integrable Tunable Laser Assembly
abstract: Multipoint sensing techniques using multimode-interference optical-fiber-sensors were investigated. System were operated using a wavelength selective optical filter and defined-wavelength-laser-light from an integrable tunable laser assembly. The average refractive index resolution of the all sensors was 3.9×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> RIU.

articleTitle: Mode detection of vector beams by use of crossed-fork-shaped polarization grating fabricated by photoalignment of photo-crosslinkable polymer liquid crystal
abstract: A crossed-fork shaped polarization grating (Crossed-FPG) was developed as a mode demultiplexer for vector beam division multiplexing communication. The Crossed-FPG was fabricated by recording several polarization holograms between optical vortex and Gaussian beam with opposite-handed circular polarizations. Mode detection of vector beams was experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optical Filter for Infrared Region Formed by Polymer Stabilized Cholesteric Liquid Crystals
abstract: We investigated the formation of optical filter for infrared region by using polymer stabilized cholesteric liquid crystals (PSCLCs) under UV irradiation conditions. The selective reflection band in infrared region in PSCLCs is expanded with the increase of UV irradiation energy, and the change of bandwidth shows the threshold characteristics for UV irradiation. The experimental results suggest that the reflection bandwidth of infrared region in PSCLCs is tunable by the UV irradiation based fabrication process. The simple polymerization technique can be applied to achieve the performance of optical filter for solar-ray in infrared regions for basis of smart windows.

articleTitle: Nano-Second Spectrometry by the Use of a Spinning Polygon Mirror
abstract: Time-resolved spectrometry was conducted by the use of a continuous-wave laser diode and an ordinary CCD-based spectrometer. These slow devices realized a temporal resolution of ~100 ns by achieving time-space conversion with a spinning polygon mirror. Decay processes of fluorescent materials were measured successfully by using this spectrometer.

articleTitle: Multiple Aerial Imaging by Use of Infinity Mirror and Oblique Retro-Reflector
abstract: This paper proposes a new optical system for aerial display applications. Our proposed system employs infinity-mirror optics for multiple imaging and forms multiple aerial images from a single light source by retro-reflection. Our proposed optics improves brightness of the aerial images by placing a retro-reflector obliquely outside the infinity mirror.

articleTitle: Manipulation of received beam for free-space optical communications of intermediate distance
abstract: For the free-space optical communications of intermediate distance, an approach to maintain the communication quality against the change of the communication distance and the unsteadiness of the attitude of the communicating partners is proposed. In this work, assuming a small body for the communicating partner, we employ the spatial light modulator instead of the conventional mechanical beam steering parts to control of the focal position of the received beam and examine the performance of beam manipulation.

articleTitle: Perforated Microring Resonators for Enhanced Sensing
abstract: We suggest that implementation of sub-wavelength gradient effective refractive index structures, first and second order Bragg grating 1D photonic crystals into silicon-on-insulator microring resonators increases the light-matter interaction and the sensitivity of bio and gas sensors. The recent results on modeling, fabrication and characterization of perforated microring resonators are presented.

articleTitle: A Self-compensating Grating Bio-sensing System for the Detection of C-Reactive Protein
abstract: For bio-sensing systems, stability is an important evaluation criterion. In this research we demonstrated a self-compensating grating bio-sensing system which compensated the coupled signal with the penetrating signal, and was able to overcome the stability problem caused by the laser power drift and to increase the sensitivity of CRP detection.

articleTitle: Observing Gravitational Waves by Laser Interferometer
abstract: Gravitational waves are generated by the violent motion of heavy mass. Therefore, gravitational waves are expected to be a very important new tool to observe the Universe such as the mergers of blackhole binaries or those of neutron star binaries. In fact, gravitational waves have been observed in the LIGO and Virgo laser interferometers. KAGRA is a project trying to observe gravitational waves with 3km×3km arm lengths laser interferometer. It has been constructed in the underground of Kamioka, Japan. KAGRA has unique features such as the underground site to minimize the effect of seismic noises and the cryogenic mirrors to reduce the thermal noises. I will discuss the status of the gravitational wave detection and the KAGRA project.

articleTitle: Miniature Integrated Spectrometer Array
abstract: We describe the design and set-up an array of micro-spectrometers for parallel sensing. The approach utilizes a prism - grating combination to obtain a linear light path and to achieve a high packing density. This yields 2'000 micro spectrometers of 6 mm length only when working with a 4/3” CCD image sensor.

articleTitle: Grating Coupler Biosensor with a Low Refractive Index Buffer Layer for Bulk and Surface Sensitivity Enhancements
abstract: We present an investigation of the use of a low refractive index buffer layer to improve the sensitivity of grating coupler biosensor for different-sized bio-molecular. Our experimental results show that the bulk and surface sensitivities can be improved by optimizing the matching conditions.

articleTitle: Snapshot-type compact multispectral imager utilizing photonic crystal multi-patterned spectral filter array
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a compact snapshot-type multispectral image sensor. The sensor consists of a CCD area sensor and a photonic crystal (PhC) type patterned spectral filter array. The perpendicular refractive index profile of the PhC roughly determines the spectral response, while the in-plane periodic structure slightly modifies it. As a result, a multi-patterned filter array with each spatial region exhibiting different transmission characteristic. The filter was directly mounted onto a CCD to construct an imaging spectrometer. Application to near infrared inspection of agricultural products (fruits) was investigated. Spectral reflectivity images at wavelengths between 610nm to 810nm were predicted with the aid of Wiener estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of High-Order Microring Resonator-Based Chebyshev Wavelength Filter Using Digital Filter Design Method
abstract: We propose a digital filter design method for a Chebyshev filter based on a high-order microring resonator (MRR). This method enables us to much more easily design an MRR Chebyshev filter with a desired 3 dB wavelength bandwidth and free spectral range, as compared with conventional design methods.

articleTitle: Wide-range Structured-Light Sensing Based on Non-mechanical VCSEL Beam Scanner
abstract: We demonstrated a scanning structured-light sensor based on non-mechanical VCSEL beam scanner, which provides relative depth accuracy of less than 1% for both short- and long-range (>5m) measurement with >200 number of lateral resolution points.

articleTitle: Subnanoscale Localization of Rare-Earth-Ion in Doped Crystal via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
abstract: We present a subnanoscale localization of three-level Λ-type rare-rarth-ion doped in crystal via coupling it to a Gaussian probe beam and a Laguerre-Gaussian control beam in the dark state of electromagnetically induced transparency. This opens a possibility for coherent manipulation and spatial selection of individual solid qubits for quantum information science applications.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Phase Modulation Scheme in Brillouin Optical Correlation Domain Reflectometry
abstract: BPSK modulation is proposed for PM scheme to reduce background in Brillouin optical correlation domain reflectometry. Effective reduction is confirmed to expand strain dynamic range both in simulation and experiment. Additionally, a new filter shape is proposed for filtering calculation scheme for the same purpose, and its effectiveness is confirmed.

articleTitle: Jacobi-Fourier phase masks to increase performance of wavefront coded optical systems for random or varying aberrations alleviation
abstract: Wavefront Coding is a technique using generalized aspheric optics and digital signal processing to greatly increase the depth of field of imaging systems. In this work we propose the use of Jacobi-Fourier shaped phase masks to produce sharp and clear images for optical systems affected by random and varying aberrations.

articleTitle: Exciton Contributed Optical Model Gain Spectra of Single ZnO Microrod by Variable Stripe Length Method
abstract: We measure the optical model gain of single Zinc Oxide microrod by Variable Stripe Length method. The pick value of gain spectra in room temperature is well below the bandgap of bulk ZnO, which comes from exciton-exciton scattering, and it can be as a reference for the design of UV-devices.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional observation of polymer and liquid crystal director in highly oriented liquid crystal / polymer composite films which show electro-optical transparency-turbidity switching
abstract: Polymer structure and azimuthal distribution of liquid crystal directors in highly oriented polymer / liquid crystal composite films were observed by using a confocal laser-scanning microscope. On the basis of the observed structure, we propose a new electro-optical mode of the composite film that the film acts as a phase modulator which generates light scattering by interference of light.

articleTitle: Optical Simulation of Diffraction Characteristics of Eccentric Fresnel Lenses for a Compact Spectrometer
abstract: Fresnel lens has a distinct wavelength dispersion for the focal lengths. This characteristic allows to apply Fresnel lens to a wavelength dispersion element for spectrometers. We have simulated the focusing characteristics of an advanced Fresnel lens which has a feature of eccentric modification to realizing a compact spectrometer.
